tool.name: MetaDAVis
tool.description: Interactive analysis and visualization of 16S and whole-metagenome sequencing results

param.name: otu_table
param.label: OTU / feature table
param.help: Feature count table in phyloseq layout: features (OTUs, ASVs or other features) in the rows, the first column holding the feature id, and one column per sample. Tab or comma separated, the separator is detected from the header.

param.name: taxonomy_table
param.label: Taxonomy table
param.help: Taxonomy assignment for the features of the OTU table: features in the rows, the first column holding the same feature ids, and one column per taxonomic rank (Kingdom to Species). Rank prefixes such as d__ or p__ are stripped. Features missing from this table are reported as Unclassified.

param.name: metadata_table
param.label: Sample metadata
param.help: Sample annotations: the first column holds the sample ids, which have to match the sample columns of the OTU table, the second column the condition/group used for comparisons. Further annotation columns are kept and shown.

tool.help:
`MetaDAVis <https://github.com/GudaLab/MetaDAVis>`_ is a browser based R Shiny application for analyzing and visualizing 16S and whole-metagenome sequencing results from kingdom to species level.
.. class:: infomark
**Results are downloaded from the browser.** Every table and plot has a download button, and the *Run* tab offers a bulk download of all analyses you have completed during the session as a single ZIP archive.
**Input datasets.** The three tables you select here are staged and pre-loaded into the application as the *Galaxy input* format in the *Upload files* tab. Open the tool, choose *Galaxy input* and press *Submit* to analyse them. The taxonomic level to display and all other options are set inside the application. You can also ignore the pre-loaded data and upload your own files from within the browser, or use the built-in example data.
What this tool provides:
#. Data summary, taxonomy and metadata tables #. Group and individual abundance distribution #. Alpha and beta diversity analysis #. Dimension reduction (PCA 2D/3D, t-SNE, UMAP) #. Correlation analysis (taxa, samples, taxa-condition) #. Heatmaps #. Differential abundance for two-group and multi-group comparisons (Wilcoxon, t-test, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, LEfSe, MaAsLin3, limma-voom, edgeR, Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA)
.. class:: infomark
**Citation**
Jagadesan S, Guda C (2025) MetaDAVis: An R shiny application for metagenomic data analysis and visualization. PLoS ONE 20(4): e0319949.
